name: Malilla
description: Malilla is a point-trick game for four players in fixed partnerships, popular in Mexico and originating in Spain. Played with a 40-card Spanish deck, the Seven is the highest card (Malilla), ranking above Ace. Partners score card points (7=5, Ace=4, King=3, Horse=2, Jack=1) plus one per trick; first team to 35 cumulative points wins. Trump is set by the dealer's last card turned face up.

content.text: Malilla is a point-trick game for four players in fixed partnerships, popular in Mexico and originating in Spain. Played with a 40-card Spanish deck, the Seven is the highest card (Malilla), ranking above Ace. Partners score card points (7=5, Ace=4, King=3, Horse=2, Jack=1) plus one per trick; first team to 35 cumulative points wins. Trump is set by the dealer's last card turned face up.
Dates back to the 16th or 17th century. Its name is derived from the word for 'little bad one', referring to the powerful low-numbered cards.
40 cards: Suits are Oros (Coins), Copas (Cups), Espadas (Swords), Bastos (Clubs).

items.text: Albur: Before first deal, one player places two cards face down; opposing team chooses one. Higher card wins 5 points and mano (right to lead to first trick). Losers deal first.

Manilla in Spain (48 cards): Played with 48 Spanish cards (eights and nines included). The nine is highest (Manilla), not the seven. Rank 9-1-12-11-10-8-7-6-5-4-3-2. 12 cards each, 12 tricks, 72 points total. Target 40 to win. No restriction on discarding a 9 of unled suit.

Macau Manilla: 40 cards from 52-card pack, rank 7-A-K-J-Q-10-9-8-6-5. Jack above Queen. Points 7=5, A=4, K=3, J=2, Q=1. No bonus for turned trump. No restriction on throwing non-trump manilla. Winning team scores difference; 70 points to win game.
